messages:
Carlos (Eng): Hey team — heads up: partner got a job in Toronto, planning to relocate in ~6 weeks. Questions on changing homebase, relocation stipend, and what payroll/benefits I need to update. Do I start a case or is there a form?

Maya (People Ops): Congrats! You'll need to file a relocation request. Short answers: 1) homebase change is required if you intend to be "ordinarily working" from Canada >30 days — but Finance uses a 90-day rule for benefits/payroll changes. 2) relocation stipend vs reimbursement depends on package. Open a People Ops case so we can review.

Carlos (Eng): We were thinking of making it permanent. What's the effect on my health insurance and 401(k? Also stock tax implications?

Rita (Benefits): If you become Canadian-resident for payroll, your US medical coverage may end and you'll be eligible for our Canada benefits package instead (provincial plan + supplemental). 401(k): contributions stop if you are off US payroll. We’ll outline rollover options and local RRSP guidance once Payroll confirms status.

June (Payroll): If you change homebase to Toronto, we need documentation (new address, work authorization). Payroll will set you up on Canadian payroll only after HR/Legal clears immigration and tax setup. Timing: expect ~40 business days for the initial checklist, longer for full payroll cutover.

Ben (Legal): Legal note: moving cross-border triggers immigration & employment law checks. If you'll do any US customer-facing contracting or supervising US hires while physically in Canada, we need to evaluate nexus and potential withholding obligations. Also equity tax withholding rules differ by jurisdiction. We'll review with Tax.

Carlos (Eng): For the relocation stipend: is it paid as a lump sum (taxable) or reimbursed for expenses? Any difference for Canada?

Maya (People Ops): Typical options: (A) lump-sum relocation payment (taxable in your payroll country), or (B) expense reimbursement (requires receipts, may be non-taxable depending on mechanism). For Canada, reimbursements still may be taxable under Canadian rules. We'll propose a package and show tax treatment.

June (Payroll): We'll need to know whether stipend is US-paid before cutover or paid after you're on Canadian payroll. If US-paid, US tax withholding applies and you may need to file Canadian returns for foreign income. We'll coordinate to minimize double withholding where possible.

Rita (Benefits): Quick checklist for benefits: 1) submit new address + anticipated first day in Canada; 2) Benefits team will pause US medical enrollment effective payroll cutover date; 3) enroll in Canada benefits during the equivalent enrollment window. We'll include contacts for brokers.

Carlos (Eng): Stock options / RSUs 1 any immediate action I should take?

Ben (Legal): Don't exercise just before cutover without tax advice. Equity tax treatment often depends on residency at vest/exercise. We'll loop in Tax and Equity Admin in the People Ops case. Avoid ad-hoc exercises until we confirm withholding rules.

Maya (People Ops): Please open a relocation case and select "international move." Attach partner job confirmation if helpful, proposed move date, and whether this is permanent. We'll issue a checklist (immigration, payroll docs, benefits forms, stipend options) and target response within 3 business days.

PeopleOps-Bot: Case created #41234 "Carlos - relocating to Toronto (partner job)". Maya will triage.

Carlos (Eng): Thanks. One more: shipping my company laptop to Canada  any export/import paperwork?

June (Payroll): IT can ship after People Ops approves and Legal confirms import rules. You may need to sign a custody and temporary import form. Keep serial numbers and declare company property at customs if required.

Ben (Legal): Also, if you will be hiring contractors or managing local contractors in Canada, flag that in the case. That activity can create a Canadian employer presence and we need to pre-approve.

Maya (People Ops): Closing loop: open the case, we'll run coordination with Payroll, Benefits, Legal, and Tax. We'll post the relocation checklist link in the case and book a 1:1 if you want help. Good luck with the move! :airplane:
